title: Incident Response and Investigations

header.html: 4.7 Summarize concepts associated with incident response activities; 4.8 Given a scenario, use data, artifacts and sources to support a security investigation
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

toc.title: Data, artifacts and sources for investigations

html:
1The incident response process

Phase What happens Key items
Preparation Be ready before an incident Training, testing, tabletop exercises (discussion-based walk-through), playbooks (step-by-step guides), simulations, roles
Identification Detect and confirm an incident Detection, internal and external advisories, threat hunting (actively searching for hidden threats)
Investigation Find what happened Digital forensics, chain of custody, e-discovery, preservation
Containment Stop the spread Quarantine and isolation of affected systems
Negotiation Dealing with an attacker (for example ransom) when decided by leadership Involve legal and executives
Eradication and recovery Remove the cause and restore systems Remove malware, patch, rebuild, restore from clean backups
Notification and external reporting Tell the right parties Stakeholders, customers, law enforcement, mandatory reporting
Post-incident Learn and improve Lessons learned, root cause analysis, post-incident reporting (PIR)
Exam tip

. The order is prepare, identify, contain, eradicate, recover, learn. Containment comes before eradication: stop the spread first, then remove. Lessons learned feed back into preparation.

2Preparation and exercises

Exercise Meaning
Tabletop exercise People talk through a scenario; low cost, no systems touched
Simulation Hands-on test with a realistic attack
Playbook Documented steps for a specific incident type
Roles Incident commander, communications, technical lead, legal

3Digital forensics concepts

Term Meaning
Digital forensics Collecting and analyzing digital evidence in a sound way
Chain of custody A record of who handled the evidence, when and why, so it stays trustworthy in court
Preservation Keep evidence unchanged (write blockers, copies, legal hold)
E-discovery Finding and producing electronic records for legal matters
Order of volatility Collect most volatile first: memory, then temporary files, then disk, then logs and archives Beyond the objectives

4Data, artifacts and sources for investigations

Source Examples
Log types Access and accounting (logical, physical), device, server, application, authentication, communication, audit, endpoint, network, metadata
Data sources Vulnerability scans, automated reports, NetFlow/IPFIX, surveillance footage, security tools, dashboards, packet captures
File and log integrity Hashes and protection show that evidence is unchanged
System image Memory dump, bit-level copy, snapshot
Stakeholders Human Resources, accounts, legal are involved when staff or money is concerned
Log-parsing techniques Searching, filtering and correlating logs to find the story
Exam tip

. A bit-level (forensic) copy keeps deleted data and slack space; a normal copy does not. Always hash the evidence and the copy. Metadata (who, when, where) is often enough to build a timeline.

Exam tip

. Chain of custody records who handled evidence; the order of volatility says to collect memory first, then disk, then logs and archives.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors finds ransomware spreading across its file servers. What should the team do FIRST?

  • ARestore from backup immediately
  • BWipe every server
  • CPublish a press release
  • DContain the affected systems by isolating them
Show the answer

Answer: D. Containment stops the spread before eradication and recovery begin.

S2Leadership wants to rehearse a data breach by discussing roles and decisions around a table, without touching systems. Which exercise fits?

  • AParallel processing
  • BPenetration test
  • CTabletop exercise
  • DFailover test
Show the answer

Answer: C. A tabletop exercise walks through a scenario in discussion form.

S3An investigator logs who collected a laptop, who held it and when it was transferred. What does this protect?

  • AData sovereignty
  • BKey escrow
  • CChain of custody
  • DRate limiting
Show the answer

Answer: C. Chain of custody records evidence handling so it stays trustworthy.

S4A responder must capture evidence from a running server. Which item should be collected first?

  • AMemory contents
  • BArchived backups
  • CPrinted reports
  • DRemote logs
Show the answer

Answer: A. Volatile data such as memory is lost first, so it is collected before disk and archives.

S5After an incident, the team meets to document what went wrong and how to improve. Which phase is this?

  • AContainment
  • BIdentification
  • CPreparation only
  • DPost-incident, lessons learned
Show the answer

Answer: D. Reviewing the incident to improve is the lessons learned and root cause part of the post-incident phase.

S6Which source shows who talked to whom on the network and how much data moved, even without packet contents?

  • AA memory dump
  • BNetFlow or IPFIX
  • CSurveillance footage
  • DA password policy report
Show the answer

Answer: B. Flow records summarize network conversations and are useful for timelines.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Name the phases of incident response in the objectives.

Show the answer

Preparation, identification, investigation, containment, negotiation, eradication and recovery, notification, post-incident.

R2What is a playbook?

Show the answer

A documented set of steps for a specific type of incident.

R3What is threat hunting?

Show the answer

Actively searching for threats that have evaded detection.

R4What does chain of custody document?

Show the answer

Who handled the evidence, when and why.

R5What is a bit-level copy?

Show the answer

An exact copy of every bit of a drive, including deleted data.

R6What does PIR stand for?

Show the answer

Post-incident reporting.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Phases prepare, identify, investigate, contain, negotiate, eradicate and recover, notify, post-incident (lessons learned, root cause)
Exercises tabletop (talk), simulation (hands-on), playbooks, roles
Forensics digital forensics, chain of custody, preservation, e-discovery, order of volatility
Sources log types, vulnerability scans, NetFlow/IPFIX, footage, packet captures, hashes, memory dump, bit-level copy, snapshot
